events.title: Designing Student Loan Programs in a Risky Economy with Lance Lochner
events.description: The Purdue University Research Center in Economics invites you to our December economic policy luncheon. Please register to hear from a Purdue Dream Hire. Designing Student Loan Programs in a Risky Economy with Lance Lochner 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. Eastern, Wednesday December 2, 2026, Rawls Hall, 3rd Floor Commons ,100 S. Grant Street, Purdue’s West Lafayette campus On average, a college education is a rewarding financial investment; yet, many students struggle in the labor market after leaving school. Some leave college with sizeable debts that are easily repaid under normal circumstances, while some find loan repayments overwhelming when luck turns against them. How do we provide enough credit to students who need it, and make sure loan obligations are repaid, on average, while providing students who face an unfavorable post-college labor market with the “insurance,” or repayment assistance, they need? Economic theory provides useful insights on the design of efficient student loan programs with empirical evidence slowly filling in the details needed to address these concerns. Professor of Economics Lance Lochner joined the Daniels School in 2026 as part of Purdue’s Moveable Dream Hires program. He is co-coordinator of the Markets Network of the Human Capital and Economic Opportunity Global Working Group, and has devoted much of his career to understanding human capital formation across the life cycle. Lochner’s major fields of concentration include labor economics, public economics, the economics of education and the economics of crime. Space is limited for PURCE luncheons, and registration is required. Please register by noon on Friday, November 27. We look forward to seeing you in Rawls Hall for a catered lunch, networking, and a Q&A with Lochner following his talk. Parking is available in the nearby Grant Street Parking Garage. Reach out to us with any questions at purce@purdue.edu and (765) 494-3782. Learn more about our research center at business.purdue.edu/centers/purce.

events.title: Executive Forum with Jennifer Richter, Vice President Supply Chain - Cleaning for The Clorox Company
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Jennifer Richter serves as the Vice President, Supply Chain for The Clorox Company's US Cleaning business unit. In this role, she leads the supply chain networks, operations, and talent that support some of the company’s most recognized household and professional cleaning brands. Her work sits at the intersection of strategies across business aspirations, suppliers, manufacturing, distribution, technology, innovation, and people leadership. The Clorox Company champions people to be well and thrive every single day. Founded in 1913 and headquartered in Oakland, California, Clorox is driven by consumer-centric innovation. From cleaning to food storage to natural personal care, the company is committed to delivering clearly superior experiences through its trusted brands including Brita®, Burt's Bees®, Clorox®, Fresh Step®, Glad®, Hidden Valley®, Kingsford®, Liquid-Plumr®, PineSol® and Purell® as well as international brands such as Chux®, Clorinda® and Poett®. With operations in about 25 countries and territories, Clorox products are sold in more than 100 countries, helping people around the world live happier, healthier lives. Having recently been named by Forbes as one of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026, Clorox is proud to be recognized for efforts and impact in areas such as corporate and social responsibility, leadership development, inclusion and diversity, and culture. Since joining The Clorox Company in 2000, Jennifer has held roles across Supply Chain Planning, Customer Service, Transportation Operations, Customer Logistics, and Manufacturing for multiple Clorox businesses. Jennifer is a passionate people leader who believes a leader’s most important responsibility is enabling others to succeed. She believes optimism is a force multiplier, principles matter more than rules, and that performance and engagement are strongest when people are able to apply their strengths. Within Supply Chain, she has implemented a leadership approach that is grounded in raising the bar while creating the clarity, confidence, and space teammates need to do their best work. With the core leadership principle of “everyone wants to succeed” in mind, she is dedicated to developing talent, implementing inclusive leadership, supply chain competency building, and career pathing for her team. Jennifer graduated from North Carolina State University with BS degrees in Chemical Engineering and Pulp & Paper Science. She lives in Atlanta, GA with her husband and two children. A local community advocate, she serves on the board of directors for the Chastain Park Conservancy, an organization dedicated to restoring, enhancing, maintaining and preserving Atlanta’s second largest public park. She also enjoys creating lifetime memories with her family and volunteering with her local faith-based organization.

events.title: ASC Workshop; Practice your POMO
events.description: Are you having difficulty with procrastination and focusing on your studies? Are you familiar with the Pomodoro Technique? The Pomodoro Technique, a popular time management method, asks you to alternate pomodoros — focused work sessions — with frequent short breaks to promote sustained concentration and stave off mental fatigue. Join the ASC in this late-night study session, on the hour, every hour with practicing the Pomodoro Technique. The workshop will include quiet work time of your choice, with frequent, short breaks in between 7pm to 11pm. The break will consist of snacks, fun trivia, and prizes which will be given out to participating students! Note: Registration is not required for Practice Your Pomo but does help with our planning.

Like studying with friends? Need absolute silence to focus? Looking for accountability to stay locked in? Have a last minute question about one of your courses? We got your covered! We are dividing the Student Center into 5 key sections: Study together in the Collab Lab, lock in at the Quiet Zone, practice a study skill in the Pomo Pod, fuel up with the Snack Shack, and get help in Tutor Town! This event has it all; energy drinks, study supplies, stress relief activities and more! Space is limited so claim your spot early and let’s tackle final exams together. This event is sponsored by Teaching & Learning and hosted by the Academic Success Center. See you there!

events.title: Sustainability from Community to Campus: A Taiwan-US Comparison of College Students’ Environmental Knowledge, Attitudes, and Behaviors
events.description: Join is for an ISF Impact Seminar! We are pleased to welcome leading sustainability expert Dr. Jane Lu (Hsu) for a discussion on Zero Waste and Sustainability. Dr. Lu is a Professor of Marketing and currently serves as Deputy Dean of International Affairs at National Chung Hsing University (NCHU), Taiwan. Her recent work includes research on community-based zero-waste practices and cross-national comparisons of environmental knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors among university students in Taiwan and the US. Date: Thursday, December 17, 2026 Time: 2 – 3 p.m. Location: MRGN 121 and Café We look forward to welcoming you, please let us know you’re coming! Register here. Hosted by: Purdue Institute for a Sustainable Future Circular Economy Systems Special Initiative and Risk and Resilience Research Community Please reach out to Tara Greene, ISF Senior Operations Administrator, at greenet@purdue.edu with any questions.

events.title: Strengthening Rural Communities: Strategies, Challenges, and Outcomes from the DRA PROPEL Initiative
events.description: In 2024, the Delta Regional Authority (DRA) partnered with the North Central Regional Center for Rural Development to support five rural communities in southern Illinois and Missouri to enhance their economic development and community resilience through the DRA PROPEL Technical Assistance Initiative. In this webinar the project’s Community Coordinators from Illinois Extension and MU Extension will share the challenges they navigated, the practices that emerged, and the tangible outcomes achieved during their two years of on-the-ground engagement with the communities. Presenters: Taylor Clark, MU Extension, Field Specialist in Community DevelopmentSusan Odum, Illinois Extension, Community and Economic Development Specialist REGISTRATION NCRCRD webinars are open to all participants. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate or need an interpreter or translator, please contact NCRCRD no later than 5 days prior to the event. NCRCRD's work is supported by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture. Past webinars are posted on the NCRCRD YouTube Channel. Purdue University is an Equal Opportunity/Equal Access University. Can’t join us live? Register anyway and you’ll receive the recording after the event.
